symptoms: Long, elliptical, cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions (2.5 to 15 cm in length)
Lesions develop dark olive to black spore mats on surfaces during damp weather
Severe infections cause leaves to wither, appear prematurely scorched or frosted
management: Manage infected maize residue through incorporation or clean field clearance where appropriate.
Rotate maize with non-cereal crops (beans, peas, soybeans, potatoes) for at least one full cycle.
If infection starts before silking on susceptible seed in highland zones, contact county extension for registered treatment protocols.
prevention: Select KALRO-recommended resistant hybrid seed varieties (e.g., H6213, H628, or modern highlands hybrids).
Maintain recommended plant spacing (typically 75 cm between rows, 25 cm between plants) to facilitate canopy aeration.
Avoid planting maize consecutively on adjacent plots with unmanaged infected stover.
monitoring: Scout lower leaves every 7 days following moderate temperatures (18-27°C) and heavy dews or rainfall.
Observe whether cigar-shaped lesions progress above the ear node.
escalation: Lesions appear on the ear leaf or flag leaf within 2 to 3 weeks of flowering.
Leaf death exceeds 30% of total canopy before the dough stage.
Neighbouring farms report severe blight outbreaks.
kenya_notes: One of the most destructive maize diseases in Kenya, particularly across Trans Nzoia, Uasin Gishu, Nandi, Bomet, and Kisii counties during wet long and short rains.
